verdict.rationale: Skyvern documents building agents via Copilot or the visual builder that you can then schedule. Those agents run in a cloud browser that handles logins, 2FA and CAPTCHAs on its own. A webhook_url posts results when a run finishes, so runs can complete in the background without supervision. missing for 10: in-depth scheduling documentation (cron/recurrence options, triggers), independent or hands-on corroboration of unattended scheduled runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Describe the job to Copilot at app.skyvern.com. It builds an agent you can test, edit in Studio, schedule and share. No code.
Pass webhook_url when you start a run. Skyvern sends one POST to that URL when the run reaches a terminal status
Save a login once and every agent can use it. Skyvern fills the username, password and 2FA code into the page for you.
Runs transparently — your automations never get stuck on verification.
You send Skyvern a prompt and a URL, Skyvern runs a cloud browser, and you get structured output back.
